title: How a Water Softener Works in 60 Seconds 🧂💧 #shorts
description:
A water softener doesn't filter your water, it trades minerals. Tiny resin beads grab the calcium and magnesium that make water hard and release sodium in their place. When the beads are full, salty brine washes them clean and the hard minerals go down the drain. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#watersoftener #hardwater #howitworks

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: A water softener doesn't filter your water. It *trades* one mineral for another.

steps.label: Hard water
steps.text: Hard water carries dissolved *calcium* and *magnesium*. They leave chalky scale in pipes, kettles and showers.

steps.label: Resin
steps.text: The water flows down through a tank packed with tiny plastic *resin beads*, each one loaded with sodium.

steps.label: Swap
steps.text: Calcium and magnesium stick to the beads more strongly, so the beads grab them and *release sodium* instead.

steps.label: Brine
steps.text: When the beads are full, *salty brine* from a second tank washes through them, usually in the middle of the night.

steps.label: Flush
steps.text: The flood of sodium knocks the hard minerals loose, and they *flush down the drain*.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Grab, *swap*, rinse. Follow Inside 60 for more.
